principles: Codex adapter files must describe Koala behavior without implying Codex runtime support that does not exist.
The recommended Codex entrypoint should be machine-checkable and easy for agents to discover.
Adapter verification should catch both missing manifest fields and accidental fake runtime assets.
drivers: User explicitly asked whether Codex needs hook/settings-like capability.
B-d308 should preserve the B-3a3b boundary that prompts mirror but hooks/settings/skills remain Claude-only.
Existing wrapper source tagging is useful but not visible as a project adapter contract.

options.name: A: Koala-managed .Codex/koala.json manifest plus wrapper verification
pros: Makes Codex adapter capability explicit and inspectable
Keeps hooks/settings absent to avoid fake runtime support
Builds on existing bin/koala-codex.js source/session tagging
cons: Introduces a Koala-specific manifest that Codex itself does not read

options.name: B: Create .Codex/hooks and .Codex/settings.json equivalents
cons: Misleads users because Codex does not consume these runtime files
Creates maintenance burden for unsupported behavior

options.name: C: Only document KOALA_ACTIVITY_SOURCE=codex without adding config
cons: Does not give projects a stable adapter contract to verify
Leaves agents to infer wrapper behavior from prose

chosen: A: Koala-managed .Codex/koala.json manifest plus wrapper verification
rationale: Choose the manifest because it gives Codex users and tests a concrete adapter contract while preserving the runtime boundary: Koala can read and document this file, but Codex is not expected to execute hooks/settings.

preMortem.scenario: Users believe .Codex/koala.json is a Codex official runtime setting
preMortem.trigger: Manifest wording says settings or hooks instead of Koala-managed adapter
preMortem.consequence: Users expect Codex to auto-trigger behavior it cannot run
preMortem.mitigation: Use explicit adapterOwner=koala and docs saying Codex does not consume hooks/settings

preMortem.scenario: Wrapper behavior drifts and stops tagging source=codex
preMortem.consequence: Codex activity becomes indistinguishable from generic CLI activity
preMortem.mitigation: entrypoint verification checks activity source/session behavior

preMortem.trigger: Someone mirrors Claude runtime assets into Codex for visual symmetry
preMortem.consequence: Project tree implies unsupported runtime hooks
preMortem.mitigation: entrypoint/codex asset tests assert those paths are absent
